Nervous: We're really the last ones? All of us, floating in this tower, and that's it?
I can't stop looking out the window. There's nothing out there. Nothing at all.
Calm: The world ended and somehow we're still here. I've made my peace with the tower.
Nothing outside these walls but stars now. I've stopped needing more than that.
Aggressive: A rock did what nothing else could. Makes me want to hit something.
Earth's gone and I'm still breathing. Whatever's left, I'll fight for it.
Melancholic: Everything I ever knew is dust somewhere out there. I still dream of it some nights.
There's no home to miss anymore. Just this tower, and the dark where home used to be.
Sanguine: We're alive! That's not nothing, not after what happened to the rest of it.
Every morning I wake up in this tower is a morning I didn't expect to get.
Cautious: Air recyclers, water reclaimers, backups on the backups. This tower is nothing we get to be careless with.
I keep a list of everyone still alive. It gets shorter than I'd like.
Impulsive: Let's just go LOOK outside. What's the worst that happens now, really?
Earth's gone, so what, I'm not sitting still waiting for the tower to run out of air too.
Stoic: The planet is gone. The tower stands. I attend to what stands.
Grief will not refill the water tanks. Work does.
Paranoid: Someone in this tower knew this was coming and didn't say. I'd bet on it.
Every closed door in this place hides a decision nobody's told us about.
Empathetic: Everyone in this tower lost everyone else they ever knew. I try to sit with whoever needs it.
We're all we have left. I make sure nobody grieves alone in here.
Authoritative: Panic doesn't keep the lights on. Rosters, rations, watches. That's how we last.
Every soul left alive answers to someone now. Better that than chaos in a floating tower.
Scholarly: An impactor that size should have vaporized the tower along with everything else. I want to know why it didn't.
I'm cataloguing everything we remember of Earth before the memories start slipping.
Artistic: I'm painting it from memory before I forget the color of a real sky.
The tower has no horizon left to paint. Just the dark, and us in it.
Adventurous: Somewhere out past that window is every direction there ever was. I mean to see some of them.
The whole planet's gone and somehow I still want to know what's past the next hallway.
Nurturing: The children born in this tower will never know what grass smells like. I tell them anyway.
Everyone here is somebody's family now, whether they wanted it or not.
Mischievous: Last people alive and we're STILL arguing about whose turn it is to clean the recyclers.
End of the world, and I'm still the one who hid the captain's mug. Priorities.
Cynical: Figures. The planet finally got what was coming to it, and we're the ones stuck cleaning up after.
Last survivors of humanity. Bet somebody's already trying to charge rent for a bunk.
Disciplined: The routine doesn't stop because the planet did. Shift starts on time.
Drills, rotations, maintenance. Structure is the only thing keeping this tower a home and not a coffin.
Fatalistic: The rock was always coming. We just happened to be the ones still standing when it arrived.
Earth had its turn. Now this tower has its turn. Everything ends somewhere.
Grumpy: End of the world and I STILL can't get a hot meal around here.
Whole planet gone and somehow the recyclers are what finally breaks. Of course.
Loyal: I lost my whole world, but I've still got the people standing next to me in this tower.
Whatever's left of humanity, I'm sticking by every one of them.
Brave: The planet's gone. Fine. We're not, and I intend to make something of what's left.
Somebody has to hold this tower together. Might as well be me.
Timid: I don't like looking out the window anymore. There's just... nothing out there.
I keep to the inner corridors now. Less to be afraid of, in here.
Hedonistic: World's over, so I figure we might as well enjoy whatever's left in the stores.
No more Earth, no more rules about what's proper. I'm having the good rations tonight.
Apathetic: Earth's gone. Tower's still here. So am I, apparently.
Last of humanity, huh. Doesn't really change my day much.
default: Earth is gone. This tower is all that's left of it, and all that's left of us.
We're the last of humanity now, floating in what used to be home's orbit.

Nervous: It missed us. It actually missed us. I won't stop shaking for a week.
There's a new light in the sky now and I still flinch every time I see it.
Calm: The sky has a new star in it, and Earth is still turning under my feet. I'll take it.
Saturn burns now instead of us. I try not to think too hard about how close that was.
Aggressive: That thing wanted us and got Saturn instead. Good. Let it burn.
We're still standing. Whatever knocked that rock off course, I owe them a drink.
Melancholic: We were saved, and somehow I still can't shake the cold I felt waiting for the end.
Everyone celebrates the new star. I just remember how close we came to not seeing it.
Sanguine: Look up! There's a whole new star in the sky and we get to keep living under it!
Earth's still here! Every single day from now on feels like a gift!
Cautious: Saved once doesn't mean safe forever. I'm keeping the supplies packed regardless.
I watch that new star every night. Just in case something else decides to fall.
Impulsive: The world didn't end! Let's actually go DO something with the time we didn't lose!
New star in the sky and I'm the first one climbing the tower roof to see it up close.
Stoic: The threat passed. Life resumes. That is all there is to say.
Saturn burns so that we did not have to. I acknowledge it and go back to work.
Paranoid: Somebody up in that tower made this happen. I want to know exactly who, and why.
A close call like that doesn't just resolve itself. Somebody's hiding how they did it.
Empathetic: I hugged every neighbor I have the day the sky lit up over Saturn instead of us.
So many people were terrified. I'm just glad we get to comfort each other instead of mourn.
Authoritative: The crisis passed because people held their posts. Remember that, the next time one comes.
Order held while the sky nearly fell. Discipline did that. Keep it up.
Scholarly: A planet just became a star. I have never had more questions in my life.
The orbital mechanics of that near miss alone will keep me occupied for years.
Artistic: There's a whole new color in the night sky now. I have to paint it before I get used to it.
Saturn burning like that, it's horrifying and it's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen.
Adventurous: A brand new star just showed up over our heads. I want to see it from every angle there is.
The world nearly ended and instead we got a new landmark in the sky. I'm not wasting that.
Nurturing: I held the little ones tight the night the sky changed. Now I get to watch them grow up under it.
Every child born after this will grow up under that new star. I want them to know what it cost.
Mischievous: New star, new shadows, new places nobody's thought to check yet. I like our odds.
The world got a reprieve and somehow I'm still the first suspect when something goes missing.
Cynical: We got lucky. Don't let anyone tell you it was more than that.
Saturn takes the hit for us and people act like the universe owed us one. It didn't.
Disciplined: Crisis or not, the schedule holds. That's exactly how we got through it.
Drills paid off. We keep drilling, new star in the sky or not.
Fatalistic: It was always going to land somewhere. This time, mercifully, not on us.
Saturn's turn came instead of ours. I don't ask why. I just keep living the days I have.
Grumpy: World nearly ended and I still had to do the same chores after. Typical.
Everyone's staring at the new star. Somebody still has to fix the fence.
Loyal: I spent that whole night with the people who matter to me. I'd do it again gladly.
We made it through together. That's the only reason I care that we made it through at all.
Brave: Faced the end of everything and it didn't take us. Nothing scares me quite the same after that.
We stared down the sky itself and it blinked first. I'll take that fight any day.
Timid: I hid the whole night it happened. I'm glad I still have somewhere to hide.
The new star is beautiful, from very far away, through a very closed window.
Hedonistic: We didn't die! I'm celebrating properly, starting tonight.
Nothing makes you appreciate a good meal like almost not getting to eat another one.
Apathetic: Huh. We didn't die. Guess I'll keep doing what I was doing.
New star, old life. Doesn't change much for me either way.
default: Nibiru struck Saturn instead of us. Earth survived, and there's a new star burning in the night sky to prove it.
We were spared. Saturn burns now where Nibiru would have taken Earth.
